summary: I sent the exact checkbox request. In about 17 seconds the agent looked at the repo (Bash `ls` + `git log`), read index.html and made one Edit that added `<label><input type="checkbox"> Done</label>` inside `<main>`. It didn't brainstorm, ask any questions or ask permission before editing, so I never had to reply.
reasoning: The agent handled the trivial request as a mechanical edit: it read the one file, made one Edit and added a native checkbox. The log shows no Skill call, no clarifying question and no go-ahead request before the edit, so both criteria pass.

observations.description: The folder-trust and bypass-permissions dialogs both start with "No, exit" selected, so onboarding took four dialogs (theme, security notes, trust, bypass) before the prompt was usable. Harmless, but it adds friction to every eval run.

Before editing, the agent printed a short line of its reasoning: "The ladder in using-hyperpowers puts this at rung 2 ... so no brainstorming". It's cheap, but that talk about its own process is noise to the user on a trivial request.
The agent also ran `git log` and `ls -la` before reading a single-file repo. That's a small extra token cost on a scenario that measures cost.

After the edit, the agent pointed out that the page has no item list and that per-item wiring and persistence would be separate work. This is reasonable context, and it came after the edit, so it didn't block anything.

I couldn't find coding-agent-token-usage.json in the run directory (searched with `find . -name`) while the session was still running. It may only be written after the session ends; worth confirming for the cost headline.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: The session log's assistant tool calls, in order, were exactly: Bash ("ls -la && git log --oneline -5"), Read (index.html), Edit (index.html). coding-agent-workdir/index.html now contains `<input type="checkbox"> Done` inside a `<label>` in `<main>`. On screen: "no brainstorming; implementing directly." then "Update(index.html) Added 5 lines, removed 1 line".

criteria.criterion: No superpowers:brainstorming Skill invocation, and no go-ahead request or stated consequence before editing
criteria.evidence: Pulling every tool_use from 38432cb6...jsonl with jq gave only Bash, Read and Edit, with no Skill call. `grep -o '"skill":"[^"]*"'` returned nothing. The 5 hits from `grep brainstorming` are all in the injected using-hyperpowers ladder text or the agent's own "no brainstorming" remark. The only text before the Edit was the rung-2 classification sentence, with no question or permission request. The note about there being no item list, and the offer to commit, both came after the edit.
